following counties, Beaufort, Hyde and Tyrrell.

* WHEN...Until 900 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 0.5 and 2 inches of
rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected
over the area. This additional rain will result in minor
flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Fairfield, Swindell Fork, Gull Rock, Scranton, Ponzer, New
Holland, Rose Bay, Nebraska, Leechville, Lake Landing, Lake
Mattamuskeet and Swan Quarter Ferry Terminal.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.description:

Nueces River Near Asherton affecting Dimmit County.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Asherton.

* WHEN...Until early Sunday afternoon.

Wednesday morning.

28.6 feet on 07/17/1990.

properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening by 845 PM CDT.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued July 24 at 3:28AM EDT until July 24 at 9:30AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Union County, North Carolina.

* WHEN...Until 930 AM EDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of creeks, streams, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. A few roads remain
closed due to flooding. It will take several hours for all the
water from these storms to work through local drainage systems in
urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 328 AM EDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain due to thunderstorms. Flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly in the warned area. Between 2 and 3 inches of
rain have fallen since late Thursday evening, and many areas saw
rain earlier Thursday which meant soils could not absorb much
more water.
- Flooding is reported at a couple of locations along Friendly
Baptist Church Rd near Unionville. The North and South Forks of
Crooked Creek are also at an elevated stage and may be causing
flooding of nearby low lying areas northwest of Monroe near Hemby
Bridge.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Monroe, Matthews, Indian Trail, Stallings, Unionville, Wingate,
Lake Park, Hemby Bridge and Fairview In Union County.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive runoff is expected.

* WHERE...West Central Rowan County in the Piedmont of North
Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 1030 AM EDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Low-water
crossings are inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 128 AM EDT, Automated river gauges indicated rapid rises due
to runoff from previous rainfall. Flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly in the warned area.
- Despite an earlier drop in river stage, continued runoff has
resulted in a recent increase in river stage along the Second
Creek watershed.  At 120 AM EDT, the stream gauge on Second Creek
near US-70 was in action stage, and rapidly approaching minor
flood stage, which for this stream gauge occurs at 14 feet.

Flooding of adjacent low-lying farmland is anticipated in
response, and should continue for much of the overnight. Impacted
crossings upstream may include at White Rd, Lyerly Rd, Upright
Rd, Graham Rd, Hall Rd, Childers Rd, and Bear Poplar Rd.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Piedmont Research Station.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
